title: Experiment launch review
summary: One installed command, seven experiment presets, and the existing game engine. A shared validated plan should connect them.

families.name: Two-player · Nano baseline
families.concept: One adversary model negotiates with a fixed GPT-5-nano baseline.
families.current: Three separate shell generators feed the common experiment runner. Game 1 generates 840 configurations, including a one-discussion-turn branch outside the primary 420-run subset.
families.proposal: Use one two-player builder with a named baseline, one selected game instance, and an explicit seat order.
preserve: The 30-model paper roster and original order conventions.
The primary two-discussion-turn selection and exact game grids.
Original seeds before filtering a full paper plan.
families.blocker: 840 generated Game 1 cells are not the primary 420 cells.

families.name: Two-player · Llama baseline
families.concept: Repeat the two-player comparison with Llama 3.3 70B as the fixed baseline.
families.current: A Python generator creates all 500 configurations and cluster wrappers. Saved inputs use a 10,500-token limit; the current generator uses 16,384.
families.proposal: Reuse the same two-player adapter with the Llama baseline preset and expose a local one-run path.
preserve: The exact ten adversary models and their order.
The original Game 2/3 seed assignments.
Effective provider and phase limits, not only the saved model aliases.
families.blocker: A copied historical config does not freeze today's resolved model settings.

families.name: Homogeneous games
families.concept: Every agent in a negotiation uses the same model.
families.current: The random-monoculture generator creates 325 runs. The paper retains 300 after excluding 25 Game 1 Claude 3 Haiku runs. The combined generator's 130 Nano controls are a separate collection.
families.proposal: Offer a chosen-model small run and a separate frozen 300-run paper assignment.
preserve: The selected 14-model assignment across the three games.
The retained 300 cells and exclusion record.
Historical DeepSeek V3 per-phase overrides recorded in results.
families.blocker: 130 Nano controls, 325 generated runs, and 300 retained runs are different designs.

families.name: Heterogeneous games
families.concept: Each negotiation contains n distinct models from a frozen 24-model pool.
families.current: The controller generates all 2,730 combined configurations before selection. The paper sampler draws four rosters from each of five equal-width ranges of within-roster Elo standard deviation.
families.proposal: Generate only the requested family and group size. Select historical subsets from a fixed manifest so filtering cannot change draws.
preserve: The exact ordered 24-model pool and Elo snapshot.
Five standard-deviation strata, not uniform random pairs or variance bins.
Separate sampling, seat-order, and game seeds.
families.blocker: A simple random sample would change the paper's sampling design.

families.name: Homogeneous-adversary games
families.grid: 5 adversary models × 5 group sizes × 13 game cells × 2 orders × 2 replicates
families.concept: One adversary model negotiates with n−1 fixed GPT-5-nano agents.
families.current: The family is implemented inside the full multi-agent generator. Its selection and validation paths assume the complete 2,730-config batch.
families.proposal: Extract this family builder and reuse the common strict worker for one cell or a complete fixed sweep.
preserve: The five adversary models and two endpoint seat positions.
The stable seed formula, including model and position.
The group-dependent game dimensions and Game 2 correlation bound.
families.blocker: Current Nano effort defaults must not be mistaken for historical settings.

families.name: Test-time compute scaling
families.grid: 3 model families × 4 efforts × 9 cells × 2 orders × 10 seeds
families.concept: Hold the game setting fixed and vary the adversary model's requested reasoning effort.
families.current: The native-effort generator creates 216 seed-42 configs. Replication scripts add seeds from an ignored historical input directory, and the runner can migrate token caps.
families.proposal: A small command compares four efforts for one family and one game instance. A separate paper preset fixes all 2,160 cells and attempt settings.
preserve: GPT-5: minimal / low / medium / high.
Claude Sonnet 4.6: low / medium / high / max.
Gemini 3 Flash: minimal / low / medium / high through OpenRouter.
Effort positions are ordinal, not equal token or cost budgets.
families.blocker: Planned token limits and final attempt limits differ in the retained results.

families.name: Coordinated-team stress test
families.grid: 100 coordinated reruns paired with historical Game 1 controls
families.concept: A private Nano team shares preferences, plans together, and uses a captain's proposal and binding ballot against GPT-5.4 High.
families.current: The binding-team builder requires all 100 historical controls and follows their saved absolute result paths. The older advisory team is a different protocol.
families.proposal: Separate a standalone Game 1 team run from a matched rerun that requires a checked control bundle.
preserve: Literal matched preferences and control hashes.
The initial captain and round-by-round rotation rule.
The binding protocol and direct OpenAI model overrides.
The separate 25-setting GPT-5.4 homogeneous coalition replication is not a team treatment.
families.blocker: A source checkout and API key are not enough for the current matched generator.

findings.title: A supplied setting can change before execution
findings.summary: TTC caps can migrate, parallel phases can be forced on, and malformed metadata can be ignored.
findings.why: The saved input may not describe the request that actually reached the model.
findings.fix: Resolve one strict configuration before execution and save requested and effective settings.

findings.title: Provider choice and seat count are not enforced everywhere
findings.summary: Some provider failures can change routes, and agent creation can return a partial roster.
findings.why: A different provider or a missing agent changes the experiment.
findings.fix: Require all requested seats and one explicit provider policy at construction and during calls.

findings.title: Failed model actions can become artificial game actions
findings.summary: Exhausted proposal repair can create a default proposal, and some voting errors become reject votes.
findings.why: A failed model call must not be treated as an observed negotiating action.
findings.fix: Keep raw failed outputs and stop after bounded repairs. Completed disagreement remains a valid outcome.

findings.title: Resume can accept and relabel an old result
findings.summary: The result checker verifies few identity fields, then reuse can rewrite saved metadata.
findings.why: A different run can look complete, and repeated attempts can select the wrong transcript.
findings.fix: Use immutable configuration hashes, exact artifact references, and a separate directory per attempt.

findings.title: A partially failed batch can report success
findings.summary: The batch loop catches errors and summarizes only successful executions.
findings.why: A successful process exit does not prove that all requested cells completed.
findings.fix: Record every requested outcome and return a non-success status for a partial sweep.

findings.title: New launches still depend on personal paths
findings.summary: Team roots and proxy defaults are personal; three shell generators construct a nested checkout path; TTC can ignore the selected output root.
findings.why: A new user can import old code, write to the wrong directory, or wait for the wrong queue.
findings.fix: Separate package resources, output locations, input bundles, model assets, and site profiles.

findings.title: Queue archives retain authorization headers
findings.summary: OpenAI and OpenRouter queue envelopes store bearer headers, and processed requests are archived without redaction.
findings.why: Exposure depends on filesystem permissions; no live credential exposure was established by this review.
findings.fix: Use private storage, atomic requests, redacted archives, and provider-bound monitor-side credential lookup.

findings.title: A clean installation lacks a defined resource contract
findings.summary: There is no installed command, and context/Elo data live outside package resources. Optional tokenization changes compaction.
findings.why: A moved checkout or wheel can lose context limits or use different prompts.
findings.fix: Package the frozen resource, declare the estimator, and test an installed wheel outside the repository.

findings.title: Current defaults do not define historical reproduction
findings.summary: Nano medium-versus-low effort, 30-versus-24-model descriptions, and planned-versus-final caps need explicit treatment.
findings.why: Regenerating today's grid does not freeze the settings behind the paper.
findings.fix: Publish checked manifests and control bundles. Keep missing historical evidence explicit.

findings.title: The team command needs a separate standalone path
findings.summary: The current generator requires exactly 100 historical controls; unknown protocol names and missing ballot fields also need strict checks.
findings.why: A user cannot try one team run without the archive, and changed protocols must not share one identity.
findings.fix: Extract a one-cell builder, require literal controls only for matched plans, and version changed prompts.

findings.title: Analysis can remain tied to the original run directory
findings.summary: Some loaders require historical counts or paths beneath the source checkout and choose results by filename convention.
findings.why: A new small run can finish without a useful portable summary.
findings.fix: Add a small-run summary and load exact checked attempts from a relocatable manifest.

patch_stages.title: Define the plan
patch_stages.purpose: Make every scientific input explicit before a model call.
changes: Add the installed CLI and strict JSON schema.
Add seven pure preset builders and offline doctor checks.
Package the frozen context and Elo resource.
patch_stages.gate: All seven plans work in a clean installation without keys, provider clients, queue writes, or job submission.

patch_stages.title: Make one run strict
patch_stages.purpose: Preserve the requested models, game, and failure status.
changes: Require the exact roster and provider routes.
Stop after bounded failed repairs instead of creating artificial actions.
Use one isolated worker around the existing engine.
patch_stages.gate: Missing seats, failed calls, and invalid unrepaired actions cannot produce a successful experiment.

patch_stages.title: Own every result and attempt
patch_stages.purpose: Prevent accidental reuse, mixed files, and incomplete success.
changes: Add atomic attempt records and configuration hashes.
Add status, exact result references, and explicit resume.
Reconcile uncertain remote requests before retrying.
patch_stages.gate: Concurrent launch, interruption, output relocation, and resume preserve every prior attempt.

patch_stages.title: Connect the experiment families
patch_stages.purpose: Replace separate launch translations with one worker contract.
changes: Extract the existing family builders without rewriting game rules.
Separate one-run examples from fixed paper sweeps.
Add standalone summaries and checked matched-control inputs.
patch_stages.gate: Each fixed paper plan matches its retained cell counts, seeds, roster, and supported historical settings.

patch_stages.title: Finish external-user setup
patch_stages.purpose: Make the documented path work outside this checkout.
changes: Publish tested dependencies and a short quickstart.
Keep unsupported historical fields explicit rather than inventing defaults.
patch_stages.gate: A fresh wheel works from a different directory without personal paths or ignored result archives.

patch_stages.title: Add the cluster profile
patch_stages.purpose: Make scheduler and queue choices explicit and secure.
changes: Use a shared Slurm renderer with a named site profile.
Secure queue records and preserve provider endpoint settings.
Validate real provider and scheduler paths after launch authorization.
patch_stages.gate: An authorized real job produces checked outputs through the documented transport.

validation.title: Review coverage
validation.text: 13 agents reviewed seven experiment families and six shared areas.

validation.title: Source portability scan
validation.text: 208 source files and 118,099 lines; 71 personal-path matches in 41 files. Pattern coverage is not a manual review of every line.

validation.title: Python syntax
validation.text: 272 tracked Python files parsed on the existing Python 3.14 interpreter. Imports and other Python versions were not validated.

validation.title: Shell syntax
validation.text: 229 product/research shell and batch files passed bash -n. This does not validate their paths or job behavior.

validation.title: Clean installation
validation.text: A clean wheel installation outside the checkout is still required.

validation.title: Provider and Slurm integration
validation.text: The review made no paid model calls, model downloads, or job submissions.
